verdict.description: approve = can be merged; reject = this pull request brings in a problem of one of the four kinds (listed in problems); needs_human = you cannot tell, a person has to look

level.description: Risk of the change itself: 0 = fix, tests, docs, refactor without behaviour change; 1 = visible UI change; 2 = a product trade-off the spec did not decide; 3 = auth, data migration, payments, secrets

problems.description: What blocks the merge, all of it in one pass, one entry each. Empty unless the verdict is reject

kind.description: logic = logic that will go wrong; criteria = an acceptance criterion (or a decision / the scope of the spec) not met; security = a security problem; tests_missing = behaviour changed and no test was added or changed

where.description: File and line in the merged code (path/to/file:123), or "PR description"

what.description: What is wrong and what it causes, one or two sentences

followups.description: Things that do not block the merge but somebody should act on afterwards, one entry each; empty list if none

kind.description: test = tests exist but do not test what they claim; existing = a defect that was there before this pull request, or the same flaw next door; summary = the plain-language summary does not match the diff; evidence = the evidence is incomplete or does not match; other = documentation, naming, anything else

what.description: Where, how to trigger it, what happens; readable by someone who never saw this pull request

ask.description: Required for level 2, level 3 and needs_human, left out otherwise: the one question the owner has to answer (level 3: what sensitive thing is touched; needs_human: what to look at), in plain words without file or function names

options.description: Required for level 2, left out otherwise: at least two ways to go; the first is what the pull request does now

recommend.description: Required for level 2, left out otherwise: the number of the option you would pick (1 = the first entry of options)

summary.description: Two sentences in plain words: what the pull request does; your verdict and its main reason
